notes: 0.3.0: the sheet formats worked out from how the core prints them, checked against the core's own printouts of a grid of formats (439 of 441 qualification cards and 684 of 684 match cards matching): any count of ends and arrows, one or two count columns (11 and 10 on a 3D face), 3D rounds of 24 ends of 2 arrows on one line each, individual, team and mixed team brackets and round robins in sets or points. On a match sheet, the rows' height follows the count of ends as the core sets it (8 mm for six ends): the Winner box of a 3D elimination no longer reads ticked when empty; the closest box of an event with eliminations is where the core prints it; the shoot-off's lines are seen on the sheet, as it was printed. A page scanned at 200 dpi is searched at its own size and at the usual one (round robin team sheets: 39 cards missed of 494 to 3; 3D qualification cards: 136 to 390 of 157 pages fitted). A grid whose outline stops a row or two short is grown to the table; small cells overrun by the writing keep their columns. A match cell without ink inside an end with arrows written is no longer taken for blank for sure: a pencil mark too faint is left to the networks and the end's total. Developer tools: a match sheet's cells in doubt go to the page of the cells to check too, and an arrow chosen in the grid is saved there as checked (not left to check again); that page can show the surest first, those read alike side by side, to be checked at a glance, and shows red an arrow typed with a value its face does not have (a 9 on a 3D face). Measured on 2,700 scanned pages of six competitions. The arrow and digit networks trained again on these scans: a 3D face's 11 is read (3D match sheets, arrows right 79 to 99 %; 3D qualification cards 84 to 97 %).
